DXaUwJhjWoe.content: Denver's Missing Middle Housing Push: Zoning Reform in Action Comment "REPORT" if you want more Colorado housing policy updates like this! Denver is advancing major zoning reforms to address housing affordability. Key Highlights: Unlocking Housing Choices (UHC): Legalizes duplexes, fourplexes, rowhomes, and cottage clusters in single-family zones. 2026 Zoning Updates: Duplexes allowed on single-family lots, limits on oversized rebuilds, and affordable housing requirements for large redevelopments. Why It Matters: Targets "missing middle" households—too high for subsidies, too low for single-family ownership. Denver's zoning has long excluded mid-scale housing. State Pressure: Colorado laws now mandate ADUs, reduced parking, and housing action plans. Debates: Critics argue new duplexes may still be expensive, density doesn't guarantee affordability, and neighborhood character could change. Big Picture: Incremental upzoning shifts Denver from exclusionary zoning toward gentle density. Whether this truly improves affordability remains uncertain. DX3eUe1jiwO.content: Thanks to @homeofva for this great poll! Let's keep working to make Richmond the best that it can be! Text: That's why we're working for zoning reform in Richmond. And we're not alone. This month, HOME of VA released results of a new poll by a nonpartisan research firm. The findings confirm what we've been hearing on the ground in Richmond: • 91% say addressing housing affordability is a top or important priority — and want City Council to act. • 73% say there is not enough housing in Richmond. • 69% support spreading development citywide rather than concentrating construction in lower-income, traditionally Black neighborhoods — as we see today. Perhaps most striking? Half of Richmond residents worry that housing costs here threaten their ability to stay long-term. Among renters, that fear rises to two-thirds. #richmond #rva #zoningreform #strongtownsrva #homesforallourneighbors

DX7rmxHBKqT.content: Today, I had the privilege of joining fellow Realtors at the State House for Realtor Day — and it was a powerful reminder of why showing up matters. 🏛️ Our industry came together to have real conversations with legislators about the issues that directly impact homeowners, buyers, sellers, and the communities we serve every day. Here's what we brought to the table: 🏠 Fair Housing & Diversity Education — Because every person deserves equal access to housing, and education is the foundation of that promise. 🏗️ Funding for Crumbling Concrete Foundations — Homeowners across the state are dealing with a crisis that threatens the structural integrity of their most valuable asset. We're fighting for solutions. 🌆 Zoning Reform & Housing Production — We need more housing, and that means updating outdated zoning laws that are blocking growth and keeping inventory dangerously low. 📋 Pre-Service Training for Local Boards & Commissions — Better-prepared local decision-makers mean smarter, faster housing decisions for our communities. And we made our opposition clear on policies that would hurt the market: 🚫 Transfer Taxes — An added burden on buyers and sellers that would slow down an already challenging market. 🚫 Rent Control — Policies that sound helpful on the surface but historically reduce housing supply and discourage investment. This is what advocacy looks like. It's not just about selling homes — it's about shaping the policies that determine whether people can find a home at all. If you have questions about any of these issues or how they might affect you, slide into my DMs. Let's talk! 💬 #RealtorDay #FairHousing #HousingForAll #ZoningReform #Realtors StateHouse RealEstate HousingPolicy CommunityFirst RealtorAdvocacy"

DYVNstAGTri.content: Love Roanoke's walkable spaces? Sign the petition and tell our city council! Requiring single-family-lots-only was a 20th century innovation that has made our spaces expensive, it's made car ownership mandatory, it's made some school districts out of reach for those with less money, and it's made our public places unsafe to walk for kids, the elderly, and everyone else. Land-use reform, the freedom to have options other than McMansions, makes beautiful, liveable, human places possible. The reason villages and corner cafes don't exist in new neighborhoods, the reason kids can't walk to school and the park is that zoning laws in recent decades made it illegal to do what people had previously done freely - work to create spaces worth living in. After the reforms passed in 2024, some with the most time, money, and influence have worked hard to keep exclusionary zoning in place. They have the votes on council as of now. But before May 18, sign the petition to say that's not what everyone wants. Even better, join us May 18 to say it directly to city council. #roanokeva #strongtowns #zoningreform Petition: https://c.org/Jt7kDHHQjj
